symbols.name: qK
symbols.def: \(q_{P^{(n)},K}(u)\) is the smallest center in \(C_{P^{(n)},K}\) attaining \(\min_{c\in C_{P^{(n)},K}}|u-c|\).

symbols.name: ZP
symbols.def: \((Z_{P^{(n)},K}:1\le K<K_n)\) is centered Gaussian with covariance \(R_{P^{(n)}}\).

symbols.name: hatGK
symbols.def: \(\widehat G_K=\widehat\rho(K+1)-\widehat\rho(K)\), where every \(\widehat W_K\) is a cross-fitted corrected loss minimized over \(\mathcal C_K\), every inverse propensity uses \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\), \(\widehat\rho(K)=1-\widehat W_K/\widehat W_1\), and every nonunique empirical minimizer is resolved by the deterministic measurable rule selecting the lexicographically smallest ordered codebook.

symbols.name: tildepsiK
symbols.def: \(\widetilde\psi_{i,K}\) is the uncentered cross-fitted plug-in value for \(\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}(O_{n,i})\), evaluated with the nuisance fits and deterministic empirical codebook selectors trained outside the fold containing unit \(i\), and with \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\) in every inverse weight.

symbols.name: hatsigmaK
symbols.def: \(\widehat\sigma_K^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K})^2\) and \(\widehat\sigma_K=\{\widehat\sigma_K^2\}^{1/2}\) is the nonnegative square root.

symbols.name: xi
symbols.def: Conditionally on the data, \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1)\) and are independent of the data.

symbols.name: qalpha
symbols.def: Let \(T_n^{\#}=\max_{1\le K<K_n:\widehat\sigma_K>0}|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}/\widehat\sigma_K|\), with the maximum over the empty set defined as zero. Then \(q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:P(T_n^{\#}\le t\mid O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n})\ge1-\alpha\}\).

symbols.name: IK
symbols.def: If \(\widehat\sigma_K>0\), then \(I_{n,K}=[\widehat G_K-q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K/\sqrt n,\widehat G_K+q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K/\sqrt n]\); if \(\widehat\sigma_K=0\), set \(I_{n,K}=\mathbb R\).

symbols.name: Bsharp
symbols.def: \(B_n^{\#}=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}I_{n,K}\) is the single data-measurable band produced by the corrected estimator and multiplier quantile.

symbols.name: PU
symbols.def:
Under \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\), \(X=U\), \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of \(U\), \(Y(1)=U-1/2+
u_n\varepsilon_1\), and \(Y(0)=1/2-U+
u_n\varepsilon_0\), with independent Rademacher marks \(\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1\).

symbols.name: Bp
symbols.def: \(B_1(t)=t-1/2\) and \(B_2(t)=t^2-t+1/6\) for \(t\in[0,1)\), extended with period one.

symbols.name: cfano
symbols.def: \(c_{\mathrm F}>0\) is fixed and sufficiently small.

symbols.name: Ptilt
symbols.def:
For \(j\in J_n\),
\[
 \frac{dP_j^{(n)}}{dP_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(o)
 =\frac{\exp\{-\delta_n s_{n,j}(o)\}}
 {\mathbb E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{-\delta_n s_{n,j}(O)\}]},
\]
and \(P_0^{(n)}=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: Un
symbols.def: \(\mathcal U_n=\{P_0^{(n)}\}\cup\{P_j^{(n)}:j\in J_n\}\), with the laws supplied by \(Ptilt\).

symbols.name: Vband
symbols.def: \(V_n\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) is independent of the sample under every row law; a procedure that does not randomize ignores this argument.

symbols.name: bandLower
symbols.def: \(L_{n,K}=L_{n,K}(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)\) is measurable and does not depend on \(P^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: bandUpper
symbols.def: \(U_{n,K}=U_{n,K}(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)\) is measurable, does not depend on \(P^{(n)}\), and satisfies \(L_{n,K}\le U_{n,K}\).

symbols.name: Bband
symbols.def: \(B_n(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\) is one common \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable map.

symbols.name: bandHalf
symbols.def: \(h_{n,K}=(U_{n,K}-L_{n,K})/2\), with \(h_{n,K}=+\infty\) when an endpoint is infinite.

symbols.name: HonestBand
symbols.type: uniform-honesty predicate over the local experiment
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\) holds when there exists a deterministic sequence \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) such that \[\inf_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\{G_{P^{(n)}}(K)\in[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\text{ for every }1\le K<K_n\}\ge1-\alpha-\eta_n.\] The probability integrates the declared auxiliary randomization.

assumptions.condition: \(\epsilon\le e_{P^{(n)}}(X)\le1-\epsilon\) almost surely for a fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\).

novel.justification: The normalization fixes a common interpretable scale for customer-level causal contrasts and is satisfied after rescaling any application with a known bounded contrast range, including binary outcomes and the uniform randomized-trial witness.

assumptions.condition: For every \(1\le K\le K_n\), \(C_{P^{(n)},K}\) is a singleton \((c_{P^{(n)},K,1},\ldots,c_{P^{(n)},K,K})\) satisfying \(0<c_{P^{(n)},K,1}<\cdots<c_{P^{(n)},K,K}<1\).

novel.justification: Unique interior population segmentations are stable for scalar feature laws with densities bounded above and below near the uniform law; the condition rules out scientifically ambiguous tied segmentations while allowing cell widths and curvature to deteriorate with resolution.

assumptions.condition: For every \(K\le K_n\) and every ordered codebook \(C\in\mathcal C_K\) with \(\min_{\pi}\|C-\pi C_{P^{(n)},K}\|_2\le\kappa_{P^{(n)},K}\), its excess distortion is at least \(\lambda_{P^{(n)},K}\min_{\pi}\|C-\pi C_{P^{(n)},K}\|_2^2\).

novel.justification: A local quadratic-growth modulus is the nonsmooth formulation of optimizer stability needed for increasing resolution; it holds for densities bounded away from zero around the uniform law and does not presume twice differentiability of the distortion.

assumptions.condition: For every \(K\le K_n\) and \(0<t\le\kappa_{P^{(n)},K}\), \(P^{(n)}[\operatorname{dist}\{b_{P^{(n)}}(X),\mathcal B_{P^{(n)},K}\}\le t s_{P^{(n)},K}]\le M_{P^{(n)},K}t^{\alpha_{P^{(n)},K}}\).

novel.justification: This resolution-indexed version of the quantization margin condition retains the shrinking cell radius and is satisfied uniformly by scalar densities bounded near the uniform density; Levrard's fixed-resolution margin condition is its geometric antecedent.

assumptions.condition: The primitive functions \(e_{P^{(n)}},\mu_{0,P^{(n)}},\mu_{1,P^{(n)}}\) admit cross-fitted estimators whose maximum \(L_2(P_X^{(n)})\) error, with uniform error for the two outcome regressions, is \(O_{P^{(n)}}(r_n)\) uniformly over the row class.

novel.justification: The lower bound isolates a nonvanishing causal-heterogeneity regime in which the ratio profile is uniformly defined; it is satisfied by the uniform witness, for which \(W(1)=1/12\), and excludes drift to a homogeneous-effect law.

Positive adjacent-score variance is the minimal coordinatewise condition for studentizing resolution gains; the exact witness calculation verifies it while allowing the raw variances to shrink at resolution-dependent rates.

definitions.name: triangular causal-quantizer class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}=\{P^{(n)}:P^{(n)}\text{ satisfies ass:consistency, ass:exchangeability, ass:overlap, ass:bounded-feature, ass:unique-interior-codebooks, ass:quadratic-growth, ass:growing-margin, ass:nuisance-estimability, ass:resolution-denominator, and ass:score-nondegeneracy for row }n\}\).

definitions.name: corrected growing-resolution profile
definitions.construction: On each validation fold, clip the fitted propensity to \([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\), insert it and the fitted outcome regressions into the corrected loss induced by \(\phi_{W,P^{(n)},K}\), minimize the empirical corrected loss over \(\mathcal C_K\) for every \(1\le K\le K_n\), select the lexicographically smallest ordered minimizer, and form \(\widehat G_K\), the raw foldwise values \(\widetilde\psi_{i,K}\), their mean \(\overline\psi_K\), the centered values \(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}\), and the nonnegative \(\widehat\sigma_K\) as declared in the symbol table.

definitions.name: common measurable rectangular band
definitions.construction: Fix one sequence of \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable maps \(B_n=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\) with \(L_{n,K}\le U_{n,K}\), coordinate half-widths \(h_{n,K}=(U_{n,K}-L_{n,K})/2\), and only the declared independent \(V_n\) as optional auxiliary randomization. Uniform honesty over \(\mathcal U_n\) means \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\) as declared in the symbol table.

definitions.name: covariance-aware multiplier band
definitions.construction: Compute \(q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\) as the conditional quantile infimum of the joint multiplier maximum over exactly the coordinates with \(\widehat\sigma_K>0\), retaining the empirical cross-resolution covariance, and report \(\{I_{n,K}:1\le K<K_n\}\), with \(I_{n,K}=\mathbb R\) when \(\widehat\sigma_K=0\). This is a single common measurable rectangular-band procedure and uses neither oracle \(P^{(n)}\)-indexed endpoints nor independent-coordinate calibration.

definitions.name: multi-resolution Fano family
definitions.construction:
Use the base law and all inward-oriented one-hot score tilts \(\{P_j^{(n)}:j\in J_n\}\), with
\[
 \frac{dP_j^{(n)}}{dP_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(o)
 =\frac{\exp\{-\delta_n s_{n,j}(o)\}}
 {\mathbb E_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{-\delta_n s_{n,j}(O)\}]},
\]
and \(P_0^{(n)}=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\).  Each likelihood is normalized separately.  The negative orientation is required before imposing a quantitative growing-resolution support-and-quantizer-stability regime; it points the first-order outcome-regression displacement inward at both endpoints.

definitions.name: warped Bernoulli-score handle
definitions.construction: Start from the probability-integral transform of the causal-feature law, expand optimized residual and loss contrasts in the transported periodic Bernoulli basis, and orthogonalize the resulting score directions against the nuisance tangent space to target the observational cross-resolution kernel.

statements.statement:
For every row \(n\), every \(0\leq
u_n\leq1/4\), and every \(K\leq K_n\), provided the fixed denominator constant satisfies \(\underline w\leq1/12\), the law \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\) satisfies the causal, support, unique-interior-codebook, local quadratic-growth, growing-margin, denominator, and score-nondegeneracy conditions of \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\). Its unique centers are \(c_{K,j}=(2j-1)/(2K)\), its boundaries are \(j/K\), and \(W_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K)=1/(12K^2)\).
statements.justification: This establishes a nonempty bounded causal experiment in which every geometric and inferential quantity is explicit.
statements.gap: Pollard1982Central and Levrard2015 analyze observed fixed-resolution quantizers, while KimKimKennedy2026 does not give a growing-resolution causal witness.
statements.consumer: MineThatData analysts obtain a calibrated benchmark for how many customer-effect segments can be distinguished under randomized-treatment noise.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(P=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\) and fix the row \(n\).  The witness construction and the mean-zero Rademacher marks give
\[
 e_P(u)=\tfrac12,\qquad
 \mu_{1,P}(u)=u-\tfrac12,\qquad
 \mu_{0,P}(u)=\tfrac12-u .
\]
Consistency holds by construction.  Since \(A\) is independent of \((U,\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1)\), conditional exchangeability holds.  The overlap inequalities follow from \(\epsilon<1/2=e_P(u)<1-\epsilon\).  Moreover,
\[
 b_P(u)=\{\mu_{1,P}(u)-\mu_{0,P}(u)+1\}/2=u,
 \qquad |\mu_{1,P}(u)-\mu_{0,P}(u)|=|2u-1|\leq1.
\]
Since \(0\leq u\leq1\) and \(0\leq\nu_n\leq1/4\), both potential outcomes, and hence \(Y\), lie in \([-3/4,3/4]\subset[-1,1]\).  The three nuisance functions displayed above are common known functions throughout the witness family, so the data-independent fits equal to those functions have error zero, which is \(O_P(r_n)\).  This proves the causal, support, and nuisance-estimability conditions.

Any ordered scalar codebook induces at most \(K\) interval cells.  Let their lengths, including zeros for empty cells, be \(p_1,\ldots,p_K\), where \(p_j\geq0\) and \(\sum_jp_j=1\).  For an interval of length \(p\), completion of the square gives
\[
 \inf_c\int_a^{a+p}(u-c)^2\,du
 =\int_a^{a+p}\left(u-a-\frac p2\right)^2du
 =\frac{p^3}{12},
\]
and the minimizer is unique when \(p>0\).  Therefore Jensen's inequality, with strictness unless all cell lengths agree, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\min_{c\in C}(U-c)^2
 \geq \frac1{12}\sum_{j=1}^Kp_j^3
 \geq\frac1{12K^2}.
\]
Equality requires \(p_j=1/K\) for every \(j\) and each center to be its cell midpoint.  Consequently
\[
 c_{K,j}=\frac{2j-1}{2K},\qquad
 \mathcal B_{P,K}=\left\{\frac jK:1\leq j<K\right\},
 \qquad W_P(K)=\frac1{12K^2}.
\]
The centers are uniquely strictly ordered and interior.  Also \(W_P(1)=1/12\), so the denominator condition holds precisely under the stated qualification \(\underline w\leq1/12\).

Near the displayed codebook, differentiation under the cell integrals is valid because the losses of adjacent centers agree at each moving Voronoi boundary.  At the optimum, for \(K\geq2\), the Hessian is
\[
 H_K=\frac1{2K}
 \begin{pmatrix}
 3&-1&0&\cdots&0\\
 -1&2&-1&\ddots&\vdots\\
 0&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&0\\
 \vdots&\ddots&-1&2&-1\\
 0&\cdots&0&-1&3
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(x\in\mathbb R^K\),
\[
 2Kx^{\mathsf T}H_Kx
 =\sum_{j=1}^{K-1}(x_{j+1}-x_j)^2+2x_1^2+2x_K^2>0
\]
unless \(x=0\); for \(K=1\), the second derivative is \(2\).  Hessian continuity therefore supplies positive \(\kappa_{P,K}\) and \(\lambda_{P,K}\) for which the required quadratic-growth inequality holds.  Because both codebooks are ordered, the rearrangement inequality makes the identity permutation minimize the permutation distance.

The maximum cell radius is \(s_{P,K}=1/(2K)\).  Choose the preceding validity radius no larger than one.  For \(0<t\leq\kappa_{P,K}\), the intervals of radius \(t/(2K)\) around the \(K-1\) boundaries are disjoint up to endpoints, and hence
\[
 P\{\operatorname{dist}(U,\mathcal B_{P,K})\leq ts_{P,K}\}
 =(K-1)t/K\leq t.
\]
Thus the margin condition holds with \(\alpha_{P,K}=1\) and \(M_{P,K}=1\).

Finally,
\[
 \zeta_P(O)=\nu_n\{A\varepsilon_1-(1-A)\varepsilon_0\},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P(\zeta_P\mid U)=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P(\zeta_P^2\mid U)=\nu_n^2.
\]
Outside the null set of cell boundaries, the periodic Bernoulli-polynomial identities are
\[
 U-q_{P,a}(U)=a^{-1}B_1(aU),\qquad
 \ell_{P,a}(U)=a^{-2}\{B_2(aU)+1/12\}.
\]
Substitution into the influence functions gives
\[
 \Delta\phi_{P,K}
 =12\sum_aw_{K,2}(a)B_2(aU)
 +24\zeta_P\sum_aw_{K,1}(a)B_1(aU),
\]
where each sum is over \(\{1,K,K+1\}\).  The two summands are uncorrelated by the conditional mean-zero identity.  Partitioning \([0,1]\) at the common grid with mesh \(1/\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), expanding the two polynomial pieces, and summing the resulting finite power sums gives
\[
 \int_0^1B_2(au)B_2(bu)\,du=\frac{\gcd(a,b)^4}{180a^2b^2}.
\]
The diagonal geometric contribution is therefore
\[
 \frac{8N_K}{5K^6(K+1)^6},\qquad
 N_K=K^8+4K^7+10K^6+16K^5+5K^4-12K^3-14K^2-6K-1.
\]
For \(x=K-1\geq0\), direct expansion yields
\[
 N_K=x^8+12x^7+66x^6+216x^5+445x^4+564x^3+402x^2+126x+3>0.
\]
Thus \(\sigma_{P,K}>0\) for every adjacent coordinate, including when \(\nu_n=0\).  All declared conditions follow.

statements.statement:
Under \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\), the complete adjacent-score covariance is \[\Sigma_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)=144H_2(K,L)+576
u_n^2H_1(K,L).\] In particular, \(\sigma_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)},K}^2=V_K^{(0)}+
u_n^2A_K\). The arithmetic kernel implies \[\sup_{\substack{K
e L\,;\ K,L\ge8}}R_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)\le0.28,\qquad d_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)\ge1.2,\] uniformly over \(
u_n\in[0,1/4]\). Thus \(J_n\) is a covariance-separated packing with \(|J_n|=(K_n-8)_+\), and universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) satisfy \[c\sqrt{\log(2+K_n)}\le w_n(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)})\le C\sqrt{\log(2+K_n)}.\]
statements.justification: The full covariance, rather than the diagonal variance or coordinate count, determines the simultaneous resolution penalty.
statements.gap: KimKimKennedy2026 supplies fixed-resolution influence functions and ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2017 supplies generic Gaussian approximation, but neither computes this arithmetic covariance kernel or its diverging packing.
statements.consumer: The covariance formula lets a MineThatData analysis replace conservative independent-coordinate calibration by the actual joint resolution geometry.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P=P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\).  Direct conditional expectation under the witness gives \(b_P(u)=u\).  For any positive integer \(a\), partitioning \([0,1]\) into the nearest-center intervals, completing the square on each interval, and applying \(\sum_{r=1}^ap_r^3\geq a^{-2}\) gives \(W_P(a)=1/(12a^2)\), with equality only at the equal-cell midpoints.  Put
\[
 r_a(u)=u-q_{P,a}(u),\qquad d_a(u)=r_a(u)^2.
\]
Since \(g_K=K^{-2}-(K+1)^{-2}\), the definitions of the two influence functions give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Delta\phi_{P,K}
 &=12\{\phi_{W,P,K}-\phi_{W,P,K+1}-g_K\phi_{W,P,1}\}\\
 &=12\{d_K(U)-d_{K+1}(U)-g_Kd_1(U)\}\\
 &\quad+24\{r_K(U)-r_{K+1}(U)-g_Kr_1(U)\}\zeta_P.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The centering constants cancel because \(W_P(K)-W_P(K+1)=g_KW_P(1)=g_K/12\).  Hence
\[
 \Delta\phi_{P,K}=12F_{K,2}(U)+24\zeta_PF_{K,1}(U),\qquad
 F_{K,p}(u)=\sum_aw_{K,p}(a)B_p(au).
\]
Repeated indices at \(K=1\) combine according to the indicator definition of \(w_{K,p}\).

For positive integers \(a,b\), partition \([0,1]\) at the common grid with mesh \(1/\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\).  On every grid interval both periodic Bernoulli functions are ordinary polynomials.  Expanding their product, integrating, and using the finite identities for \(\sum r\), \(\sum r^2\), \(\sum r^3\), and \(\sum r^4\) gives
\[
 \int_0^1B_1(au)B_1(bu)\,du=\frac{\gcd(a,b)^2}{12ab},\qquad
 \int_0^1B_2(au)B_2(bu)\,du=\frac{\gcd(a,b)^4}{180a^2b^2}.
\]
To expose the cancellation, write \(a=da_0,b=db_0\) with coprime \(a_0,b_0\).  Grouping the \(da_0b_0\) grid intervals by their residues modulo \(a_0\) and \(b_0\) leaves factors \(d^2/(ab)\) for \(B_1\) and \(d^4/(a^2b^2)\) for \(B_2\); direct integration on \([0,1]\) supplies \(\int B_1^2=1/12\) and \(\int B_2^2=1/180\).  This proves the two displayed identities without an external analytic result.

The conditional mean-zero and variance identities for \(\zeta_P\) make the two components uncorrelated.  Thus
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Sigma_P(K,L)
 &=144\int_0^1F_{K,2}F_{L,2}
 +576\nu_n^2\int_0^1F_{K,1}F_{L,1}\\
 &=144H_2(K,L)+576\nu_n^2H_1(K,L).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Expanding the diagonal and using \(\gcd(K,K+1)=1\) gives
\[
 H_1(K,K)=\frac{(K^2+K+1)(2K^4+4K^3-K^2-3K-1)}
 {12K^4(K+1)^4},
\]
\[
 H_2(K,K)=\frac{K^8+4K^7+10K^6+16K^5+5K^4-12K^3-14K^2-6K-1}
 {90K^6(K+1)^6}.
\]
Multiplication by \(576\nu_n^2\) and \(144\), respectively, proves \(\sigma_{P,K}^2=V_K^{(0)}+\nu_n^2A_K\).

We next certify the numerical separation.  Set
\[
 \Gamma_p(K,L)=\frac{H_p(K,L)}{\{H_p(K,K)H_p(L,L)\}^{1/2}}.
\]
For \(k\geq8\), direct clearing of the positive denominators gives
\[
 H_1(k,k)\geq\frac7{48k^2},\qquad H_2(k,k)\geq\frac1{109k^4}.
\]
After writing \(x=k-8\), the two numerator differences are, respectively,
\[
 x^6+44x^5+778x^4+6948x^3+31813x^2+63808x+24764
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 19x^8+1112x^7+27964x^6+392456x^5+3331355x^4
 +17229864x^3\\
 {}+51279088x^2+73631346x+26318627,
 \end{aligned}
\]
so both are nonnegative.

Assume \(8\leq K<L\), put \(t=K/L\), and use \(g_k\leq2/k^3\).  In \(H_1(K,L)\), the three positive frequency-one terms, after division by the diagonal lower bound, total at most
\[
 \frac47\left\{\frac4{K^2L^2}+\frac2{K^2L}+\frac2{KL^2}\right\}
 \leq\frac{19}{4536}<\frac3{700}.
\]
If neither \(K\mid L\) nor \(K+1\mid L+1\), each remaining positive greatest-common-divisor term is a proper divisor and hence at most half its smaller argument.  If \(t\leq19/20\), their normalized sum is at most \(2t/7\), and
\[
 \Gamma_1(K,L)\leq19/70+3/700=193/700<7/25.
\]
If \(t>19/20\), \(h=L-K<K/19\) bounds both greatest common divisors, so their normalized sum is less than \(8/(7\cdot19^2)\); adding \(3/700\) is again below \(7/25\).

If \(K\mid L\), write \(L=qK\).  For \(q\geq3\), the first main term is at most \(4/(7q)\).  The other greatest common divisor is \(\gcd(K+1,q-1)\), and
\[
 \frac{\min(q-1,K+1)^2}{q}\leq K+1,
\]
so its contribution is at most \(4/\{7(K+1)\}\).  Including the frequency-one terms gives at most \(16/63+3/700<7/25\).  The case \(K+1\mid L+1\) is symmetric.  Only \(L=2K\) and \(L=2K+1\) remain.  Direct substitution gives
\[
 H_1(K,2K)=
 \begin{cases}
 (K-1)(K+1)/(48K^4),&K\text{ even},\\
 (K^4+2K^3-3K^2-2K-1)/\{48K^4(K+1)^2\},&K\text{ odd},
 \end{cases}
\]
\[
 H_1(K,2K+1)=
 \begin{cases}
 (K^4+2K^3-3K^2-6K-3)/\{48K^2(K+1)^4\},&K\text{ even},\\
 K(K+2)/\{48(K+1)^4\},&K\text{ odd}.
 \end{cases}
\]
After substitution of the diagonal formula, clearing the positive denominators, and writing \(x=K-8\), the four differences \((7/25)^2H_1(K,K)H_1(L,L)-H_1(K,L)^2\) have numerator coefficient vectors
\[
\begin{split}
 &(2544,240672,10393928,270870520,4742210135,58729915892,527271838246,3455262502406,\\
 &\quad16388732574185,54811597404220,122528488405133,164090221734096,99322453821696),\\
 &(2544,240672,10453928,275910520,4932530135,62984545892,589628026996,4081319864906,\\
 &\quad20749481238560,75619391746720,187621442781383,284640797514096,199687969101696),\\
 &(2544,278304,13972520,425483640,8748325655,127895513844,1362728652524,10659476141778,\\
 &\quad60735769607880,245783723516520,670424622710535,1106577747715608,835717237221492),\\
 &(2544,278304,13912520,420323640,8548825655,123329183844,1294207073774,9955128761778,\\
 &\quad55713169654755,221251056581520,591874592859285,957709168083108,708907772727117).
\end{split}
\]
All coefficients are positive, proving \(\Gamma_1(K,L)\leq7/25\).

For \(p=2\), the frequency-one terms are bounded after standardization by
\[
 \frac{109}{180}\left\{\frac4{KL}
 +\frac{2L^2}{K(L+1)^4}+\frac{2K^2}{L(K+1)^4}\right\}
 \leq\frac1{25},
\]
where the right side is maximized at \((K,L)=(8,9)\).  With neither divisibility, the main terms are at most \(109/1440\).  Under divisibility with quotient \(q\geq3\), they are at most
\[
 \frac{109}{180q^2}+\frac{109(K+2)^2}{180(K+1)^4}<\frac4{25};
\]
for \(q=2\), the companion greatest common divisor is at most \(2\), and direct substitution yields the same bound.  Hence \(\Gamma_2(K,L)\leq1/5<7/25\).  All divisions are valid by the diagonal positivity proved above.

Cauchy--Schwarz in \(\mathbb R^2\) now gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Sigma_P(K,L)
 &\leq\frac7{25}\left[144\{H_2(K,K)H_2(L,L)\}^{1/2}
 +576\nu_n^2\{H_1(K,K)H_1(L,L)\}^{1/2}\right]\\
 &\leq\frac7{25}\{\sigma_{P,K}^2\sigma_{P,L}^2\}^{1/2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(R_P(K,L)\leq0.28\) and \(d_P(K,L)\geq\sqrt{1.44}=1.2\).

Let \(m=|J_n|=(K_n-8)_+\).  For \(m\geq2\), compare \(Z=(Z_{P,K}:K\in J_n)\) with \(Y_K=\sqrt{0.72}\varepsilon_K+\sqrt{0.28}\varepsilon_0\), where all Gaussian variables on the right are independent and standard normal.  Their marginal variances agree, while \(R_P(K,L)\leq0.28=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_K,Y_L)\) off the diagonal.  For \(f_\beta(x)=\beta^{-1}\log\sum_Ke^{\beta x_K}\), Gaussian integration by parts along \(\sqrt tZ+\sqrt{1-t}Y\) gives
\[
 \frac d{dt}\mathbb Ef_\beta
 =\frac12\sum_{K,L}(R_P(K,L)-R_Y(K,L))
 \mathbb E(\partial_{KL}f_\beta)\geq0,
\]
because diagonal differences vanish and \(\partial_{KL}f_\beta=-\beta p_Kp_L\leq0\) off the diagonal.  Letting \(\beta\to\infty\),
\[
 \mathbb E\max_{K\in J_n}Z_{P,K}
 \geq\sqrt{0.72}\,\mathbb E\max_{j\leq m}\varepsilon_j.
\]
Integrating the Gaussian density on \([t,t+t^{-1}]\) gives \(1-\Phi(t)\geq ct^{-1}e^{-t^2/2}\) for \(t\geq1\).  Therefore, with \(M_m=\max_{j\leq m}\varepsilon_j\),
\[
 \mathbb P(M_m\geq t)=1-\Phi(t)^m
 \geq1-\exp\{-m(1-\Phi(t))\}.
\]
Also \(M_m\geq\varepsilon_1\), whence
\[
 \mathbb EM_m\geq t\mathbb P(M_m\geq t)-\mathbb E(-\varepsilon_1)_+.
\]
Taking \(t=\sqrt{\log m}\), and reducing the constant to absorb finitely many small \(m\), yields \(\mathbb EM_m\geq c'\sqrt{\log m}\).  Since \(\max|Z_K|\geq\max_{K\in J_n}Z_K\), this proves the lower width bound for diverging \(K_n\).  For bounded \(K_n\), reduce the constant once more and use \(\mathbb E|Z_{P,1}|=\sqrt{2/\pi}\).

For the upper bound, the Gaussian moment-generating function gives, for every \(s>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\max_{1\leq K<K_n}|Z_{P,K}|
 \leq\frac{\log\{2(K_n-1)\}}s+\frac s2.
\]
Choosing \(s=\sqrt{2\log\{2(K_n-1)\}}\) completes the upper bound.

statements.statement:
Set \(\nu_n=0\) in \(\mathcal U_n\), and suppose the fixed class denominator satisfies \(\underline w\leq1/12\).  In \(\texttt{def:corrected-profile-estimator}\), use a fixed finite number of deterministic folds whose training sizes are at least a fixed positive fraction of \(n\), and use the common known nuisance functions \(e(u)=1/2\), \(\mu_1(u)=u-1/2\), and \(\mu_0(u)=1/2-u\), so that \(r_n=0\).  If \(\delta_nK_n^5\to0\) and \(K_n^5L_n\to0\), then, uniformly over \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n\), every empirical codebook selected by the estimator enters its population quadratic-growth basin and has ordered Euclidean displacement \(O_{P^{(n)}}(\delta^C_{P^{(n)},K,n})\), simultaneously over \(K\leq K_n\).  Moreover,
\[
 \max_{1\leq K<K_n}\frac{|\widehat G_K-G_{P^{(n)}}(K)-(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}-P^{(n)})\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}|}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}
 =O_{P^{(n)}}\!\left(\max_{K<K_n}\frac{R^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}\right),
\]
and the maximum coordinatewise \(L_2(P^{(n)})\) discrepancy between \(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\) and \(\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}(O_{n,i})/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\) is
\[
 O_{P^{(n)}}\!\left(\max_{K<K_n}\frac{S^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}\right).
\]
If additionally \(\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\Xi_n(P^{(n)})\to0\), then
\[
 \max_{1\leq K<K_n}\left|\frac{\widehat\sigma_K}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}-1\right|=o_{P^{(n)}}(1)
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal U_n\), \(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\) with probability tending to one uniformly, and all reoptimization, score-estimation, and variance-estimation effects on the studentized maximum are negligible on the intrinsic Gaussian-width scale.
statements.justification: The theorem derives empirical basin entry and the corrected reoptimization remainder on the explicit local experiment where a uniform global gap is available.
statements.gap: The fixed- or level-by-level quantizer results in Pollard1982Central, Levrard2015, and LiuPages2020 do not supply simultaneous shrinking-score linearization for a corrected causal profile.
statements.consumer: The derived remainder comparison tells MineThatData analysts whether codebook fitting reaches the local basin before joint uncertainty dominates.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a law \(P=P_j^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n\) with \(\nu_n=0\).  The density and optimizer bounds in \(\texttt{thm:fano-membership}\) are uniform in \(j\), including \(j=0\).  In particular,
\[
 cK^{-2}\leq W_P(K)\leq CK^{-2},\quad
 \lambda_{P,K}\geq cK^{-3},\quad s_{P,K}\asymp K^{-1},\quad
 \sigma_{P,K}\asymp K^{-2}. \tag{17}
\]

We first prove empirical basin entry.  For an ordered codebook \(C\), the function \(u\mapsto\ell_C(u)=\min_{c\in C}(u-c)^2\) is continuous, is absolutely continuous between finitely many boundaries, and has derivative bounded in absolute value by two.  Integration by parts therefore gives, for every empirical distribution function \(F_N\) and its population counterpart \(F_P\),
\[
 \sup_{C\in\mathcal C_K}|(P_N-P)\ell_C|
 \leq2\|F_N-F_P\|_\infty. \tag{18}
\]
For a fixed \(x\), the indicator variables \(\mathbf1\{U_i\leq x\}\) are bounded Bernoulli variables.  Choose deterministic population quantiles whose distribution-function values are the grid \(\{r/N:0\leq r\leq N\}\).  Monotonicity of both distribution functions bounds the supremum between adjacent grid points by the larger endpoint error plus \(1/N\).  Applying the exponential Markov inequality to the centered Bernoulli sums at the grid points and taking a union bound yields
\[
 \mathbb P_P\{\|F_N-F_P\|_\infty>t+N^{-1}\}\leq2(N+1)e^{-2Nt^2}. \tag{19}
\]
Every training size is at least \(c_{\mathrm{tr}}n\), and the number of folds is fixed.  Taking \(t=C L_n\) in (18)--(19) shows that their left side is \(O_P(L_n)\), simultaneously over all folds, laws, and \(K\leq K_n\).  The population proof leading to (6), transferred by the density bound (2), gives an off-basin population gap \(cK^{-5}\).  Since \(K_n^5L_n\to0\), (18)--(19) force every empirical minimizer into the population basin with probability tending to one uniformly.  This establishes global entry before local quadratic growth is invoked.

Inside that basin, put \(C_{P,K}=C^star\) and \(d(C)=\|C-C^star\|_2\).  For one observation, the directional derivative of the loss is \(2\{c_r-U\}v_r\) on cell \(r\).  The disjoint cells, (17), and \(|c_r-U|\leq C/K\) give
\[
 E_P\left[\left\{\left.\frac d{dt}\ell_{C^star+tv}(U)\right|_{t=0}\right\}^2\right]
 \leq CW_P(K)\|v\|_2^2. \tag{20}
\]
The centered moment-generating-function inequality for bounded variables, applied to the cellwise gradient vector and followed by a dyadic peeling over \(d(C)\), yields, with probability at least \(1-2e^{-x}\),
\[
 \sup_{d(C)\leq r}|(P_N-P)(\ell_C-\ell_{C^star})|
 \leq C\left\{r\sqrt{\frac{W_P(K)(x+\log(nK_n))}{n}}
 +\frac{r^2(x+\log(nK_n))}{n}\right\}. \tag{21}
\]
To see that no dimension factor is hidden in (21), square the cellwise gradient norm before taking expectation: by disjointness, the sum of its \(K\) coordinate variances is \(4E_P\{U-q_{P,K}(U)\}^2=4W_P(K)\).  The boundary-switching remainder is quadratic because the two adjacent squared losses agree at their common boundary, and is absorbed by the second term.  Thus (21) follows directly from the scalar exponential bound on each dyadic shell and a union bound over \(K\) and the fixed folds.

The population quadratic-growth inequality and empirical optimality imply
\[
 \lambda_{P,K}d(\widehat C_K)^2
 \leq |(P_N-P)(\ell_{\widehat C_K}-\ell_{C^star})|.
\]
Substitution of (21), absorption of the quadratic term using \(K_n^5L_n\to0\), and division by the positive \(\lambda_{P,K}\) give
\[
 d(\widehat C_K)
 =O_P\left[\lambda_{P,K}^{-1}
 \left\{\frac{W_P(K)\log(nK_n)}n\right\}^{1/2}\right]
 =O_P(\delta^C_{P,K,n}) \tag{22}
\]
simultaneously.  A second use of (21) gives the optimized-risk remainder
\[
 \left|\widehat W_K-W_P(K)-(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}-P)\phi_{W,P,K}\right|
 =O_P\left\{\frac{W_P(K)\log(nK_n)}{n\lambda_{P,K}}\right\}
 =O_P(R_{P,K,n}), \tag{23}
\]
where the nuisance terms in \(R_{P,K,n}\) vanish because the common nuisances are used exactly.  Equation (23) is uniform over folds and resolutions.

Write \(\widehat W_a=W_P(a)+Z_a+e_a\), where \(Z_a=(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}-P)\phi_{W,P,a}\), \(|e_a|=O_P(R_{P,a,n})\), and \(|Z_a|=O_P(L_n)\) uniformly by boundedness and the same exponential argument.  Since \(W_P(1)\geq1/24\) and \(|Z_1+e_1|=o_P(1)\), the exact identity
\[
 \frac{x+u}{y+v}-\frac xy-\frac uy+\frac{xv}{y^2}
 =-\frac{uv}{y(y+v)}+\frac{xv^2}{y^2(y+v)} \tag{24}
\]
is valid with \(y=W_P(1)\).  Apply (24) first to \(W_P(K)/W_P(1)\) and then to \(W_P(K+1)/W_P(1)\).  The linear terms combine to \((P_{\mathrm{emp},n}-P)\Delta\phi_{P,K}\), while the four displayed remainder types are exactly bounded by the four terms defining \(R^G_{P,K,n}\).  This proves the asserted gain expansion.

It remains to control fitted scores.  On the event (22), a point can change its nearest center only if it lies within \(2\delta^C_{P,K,n}\) of a population Voronoi boundary.  Off this switching set the residual-map discrepancy is at most \(\delta^C_{P,K,n}\); on it both residuals are at most \(2s_{P,K}\).  The margin inequality therefore gives
\[
 \|\{U-q_{\widehat C_K}(U)\}-\{U-q_{P,K}(U)\}\|_{L_2(P)}^2
 \leq (\delta^C_{P,K,n})^2
 +16M_{P,K}s_{P,K}^2
 \left(\frac{\delta^C_{P,K,n}}{s_{P,K}}\right)^{\alpha_{P,K}}, \tag{25}
\]
when the validity condition in the definition of \(Q^C_{P,K,n}\) holds; otherwise the trivial unit bound applies.  Thus (25) is bounded by \((Q^C_{P,K,n})^2\) in both cases.  Substitution into the ratio influence-function formula, followed by the triangle inequality, gives exactly the four codebook terms in the corrected \(S^G_{P,K,n}\); the nuisance terms are zero here.  Centering by \(\overline\psi_K\) adds no larger order, because its oracle part is controlled by the bounded-score empirical mean and its fitted-minus-oracle part by the same \(L_2\) bound.  This proves the score-discrepancy assertion.

By (1), (15), and (22), the oracle standardized scores are uniformly bounded on the local experiment.  Applying the bounded-variable exponential inequality to their squares gives
\[
 \max_{K<K_n}|P_{\mathrm{emp},n}s_{P,K}^2-1|=O_P\{\sqrt{\log(nK_n)/n}\}=o_P(1). \tag{26}
\]
The difference of two empirical second moments is bounded by the product of the empirical \(L_2\) norm of the score difference and the sum of the two empirical \(L_2\) norms.  Hence (25)--(26) and \(\Xi_n(P)\to0\) imply \(\max_K|\widehat\sigma_K/\sigma_{P,K}-1|=o_P(1)\).  Positivity of every \(\widehat\sigma_K\) follows with probability tending to one from (17).  Finally, the definition of \(\Xi_n\) multiplies the gain remainder and score discrepancy by the Gaussian-width and anti-concentration scales needed for the maximum.  Its convergence to zero therefore makes all three feasible-oracle replacements negligible on that scale, as claimed.

Let \(\nu_n=0\), suppose the fixed class denominator satisfies \(\underline w\leq1/12\), suppose \(|J_n|\geq2\) eventually, and suppose \(\delta_nK_n^5\to0\).  Then every likelihood in \(\texttt{def:fano-family}\) is normalized and has the same support, treatment mechanism, conditional outcome laws, causal feature \(b(u)=u\), and oracle nuisance functions as \(P_0^{(n)}=P_{U,0}^{(n)}\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), every \(P_j^{(n)}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\), with constants uniform in \(j\in J_n\): its feature density \(f_{n,j}\) satisfies \(\|f_{n,j}-1\|_\infty\leq C\delta_n\); its population codebooks are unique and obey
\[
 \|C_{P_j^{(n)},K}-C_{P_0^{(n)},K}\|_2\leq C\delta_nK^{3/2},\quad
 \lambda_{P_j^{(n)},K}\geq cK^{-3},\quad
 s_{P_j^{(n)},K}\asymp K^{-1},
\]
and one may take \(\kappa_{P_j^{(n)},K}=c/K\), \(\alpha_{P_j^{(n)},K}=1\), and \(M_{P_j^{(n)},K}\leq C\), uniformly over \(1\leq K\leq K_n\).  Moreover,
\[
 \max_{K<K_n}\left|\frac{\sigma_{P_j^{(n)},K}}{\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}}-1\right|
 +\sup_{K,L<K_n}|R_{P_j^{(n)}}(K,L)-R_{P_0^{(n)}}(K,L)|
 \leq C\delta_nK_n^5=o(1),
\]
and, uniformly over \(K<K_n\),
\[
 G_{P_j^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_0^{(n)}}(K)
 =-\delta_n\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}R_{P_0^{(n)}}(K,j)
 +O\!\left(\delta_n^2K_n^5\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}\right).
\]
There is a fixed \(a_0>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \min_{j\ne\ell\,;\ j,\ell\in J_n}\max_{K\in J_n}
 \frac{|G_{P_j^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_\ell^{(n)}}(K)|}{\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}}
 \geq a_0\delta_n,
\]
and \(\operatorname{KL}\{(P_j^{(n)})^{\otimes n},(P_0^{(n)})^{\otimes n}\}\leq Cn\delta_n^2\).
statements.justification: The noiseless inward score tilt supplies a genuine within-class multi-resolution experiment with explicit optimizer, covariance, likelihood, and gain-separation control.
statements.gap: Levrard2015 gives a fixed-resolution excess-distortion lower-bound construction; it does not certify a growing observed-data causal likelihood packing aligned with adjacent efficient-score directions.
statements.consumer: The result makes failure of fine MineThatData resolution reports information-theoretic, while explicitly limiting that conclusion to the bounded-feature-safe noiseless local experiment.
statements.proof_tex:
Throughout this proof set \(P_0=P_{U,0}^{(n)}\).  At \(\nu_n=0\), the witness calculation gives \(\zeta_{P_0}=0\) and
\[
 s_{n,j}(U)=\frac{12F_{j,2}(U)}{\sigma_{P_0,j}},\qquad
 F_{j,2}(u)=\sum_aw_{j,2}(a)B_2(au).
\]
Because \(\|B_2\|_\infty\leq1/6\), \(g_j\leq2j^{-3}\), and the diagonal formula in \(\texttt{thm:exact-covariance-packing}\) gives \(c j^{-4}\leq\sigma_{P_0,j}^2\leq Cj^{-4}\),
\[
 \sup_{j\geq8}\|s_{n,j}\|_\infty\leq C_s,\qquad
 E_{P_0}s_{n,j}=0,\qquad E_{P_0}s_{n,j}^2=1. \tag{1}
\]
For \(0\leq t\leq\delta_n\), define
\[
 f_{t,j}(u)=\frac{e^{-t s_{n,j}(u)}}{Z_{t,j}},\qquad
 Z_{t,j}=\int_0^1e^{-t s_{n,j}(v)}\,dv.
\]
Equation (1) implies \(e^{-C_st}\leq Z_{t,j}\leq e^{C_st}\), and therefore
\[
 e^{-2C_st}\leq f_{t,j}(u)\leq e^{2C_st},\qquad
 \|f_{t,j}-1\|_\infty\leq C t. \tag{2}
\]
This proves normalization and common support.  Since the likelihood ratio is a function of \(U=X\) only, conditioning on \(U=u\) cancels it.  Hence
\[
 e_{P_{t,j}}(u)=\tfrac12,\quad
 \mu_{1,P_{t,j}}(u)=u-\tfrac12,\quad
 \mu_{0,P_{t,j}}(u)=\tfrac12-u,\quad b_{P_{t,j}}(u)=u. \tag{3}
\]
Thus consistency, exchangeability, overlap, bounded feature support, bounded outcomes, and zero-error nuisance estimability are preserved exactly.  In particular, the endpoint failure of the positive noisy tilt cannot occur here.

We next prove global optimizer stability.  Let \(Q_{0,K}(C)=\int_0^1\min_{c\in C}(u-c)^2du\), let \(C_K^0\) be the equal-cell codebook, let \(p_r\) be the Voronoi-cell lengths of an ordered \(C\), and let \(e_r\) be the difference between \(c_r\) and its cell midpoint.  Completion of the square and the identity
\[
 \sum_{r=1}^Kp_r^3-K^{-2}
 =\sum_{r=1}^K(p_r-K^{-1})^2(p_r+2K^{-1})
\]
give
\[
 Q_{0,K}(C)-Q_{0,K}(C_K^0)
 \geq\frac1{6K}\sum_r(p_r-K^{-1})^2+\sum_rp_re_r^2. \tag{4}
\]
If every \(p_r\geq1/(2K)\), then
\[
 |c_r-c_{K,r}^0|
 \leq |e_r|+\sum_{q<r}|p_q-K^{-1}|+\tfrac12|p_r-K^{-1}|,
\]
so Cauchy--Schwarz and (4) yield
\[
 Q_{0,K}(C)-Q_{0,K}(C_K^0)\geq cK^{-3}\|C-C_K^0\|_2^2. \tag{5}
\]
If some \(p_r<1/(2K)\), the first term in (4) is at least \(1/(24K^3)\).  Combining the cases proves the global coercivity bound
\[
 Q_{0,K}(C)-Q_{0,K}(C_K^0)
 \geq cK^{-3}\min\{\|C-C_K^0\|_2^2,K^{-2}\}. \tag{6}
\]
This is the required off-basin conclusion: outside any fixed multiple of \(K^{-1}\) in ordered Euclidean distance, the gap is at least \(cK^{-5}\).

Let \(Q_{t,j,K}(C)=\int\min_{c\in C}(u-c)^2f_{t,j}(u)du\), and let \(C_{t,j,K}\) be a minimizer, which exists by compactness of \(\mathcal C_K\).  From (2),
\[
 (1-Ct)Q_{0,K}(C)\leq Q_{t,j,K}(C)\leq(1+Ct)Q_{0,K}(C). \tag{7}
\]
Optimality, (7), and \(Q_{0,K}(C_K^0)=1/(12K^2)\) imply
\[
 Q_{0,K}(C_{t,j,K})-Q_{0,K}(C_K^0)\leq CtK^{-2}. \tag{8}
\]
Equations (6)--(8) show that all minimizers enter the regular neighborhood \(\|C-C_K^0\|_2<c_0/K\) whenever \(tK^3\) is sufficiently small.  This is a derived basin-entry statement, not an assumption.

For a codebook in that neighborhood all consecutive gaps and both endpoint distances are between fixed multiples of \(K^{-1}\).  Differentiating the cell integrals is legitimate because adjacent squared losses coincide at the moving boundaries.  For the uniform law the Hessian quadratic form can be written
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}H_{0,K}(C)x
 =2c_1x_1^2+2(1-c_K)x_K^2
 +\frac12\sum_{r=1}^{K-1}(c_{r+1}-c_r)(x_{r+1}-x_r)^2. \tag{9}
\]
The discrete inequality
\[
 \sum_{r=1}^Kx_r^2\leq C K^2
 \left\{x_1^2+x_K^2+\sum_{r=1}^{K-1}(x_{r+1}-x_r)^2\right\}
\]
therefore gives \(x^{\mathsf T}H_{0,K}(C)x\geq cK^{-3}\|x\|_2^2\).  The formula for the perturbed Hessian consists of cell probabilities and boundary-density values.  Equation (2) consequently gives
\[
 |x^{\mathsf T}\{H_{t,j,K}(C)-H_{0,K}(C)\}x|
 \leq CtK^{-1}\|x\|_2^2. \tag{10}
\]
Since \(tK^2=o(1)\) under the stated regime, (9)--(10) show that the perturbed Hessian is bounded below by \(cK^{-3}I_K\) throughout the regular neighborhood.

At \(C_K^0\), the uniform part of the gradient vanishes.  Each of the \(K\) cell-gradient coordinates is bounded, by (2), by \(Ct/K^2\); hence
\[
 \|\nabla Q_{t,j,K}(C_K^0)\|_2\leq CtK^{-3/2}. \tag{11}
\]
The mean-value identity, (10), and (11) now yield
\[
 \|C_{t,j,K}-C_K^0\|_2
 \leq CK^3\|\nabla Q_{t,j,K}(C_K^0)\|_2
 \leq CtK^{3/2}. \tag{12}
\]
Strict positivity of the Hessian and the global basin entry make this minimizer unique.  Under \(tK_n^5=o(1)\), (12) is small compared with the \(K^{-1}\) cell scale.  Thus the centers remain interior and strictly ordered, \(s_{P_{t,j},K}\asymp K^{-1}\), and (9)--(10) give quadratic growth with \(\lambda_{P_{t,j},K}\geq cK^{-3}\) on a radius \(c/K\).

By (2), the density is at most two for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The union of radius \(ts_{P_{t,j},K}\) neighborhoods of the \(K-1\) boundaries has Lebesgue measure at most \(2(K-1)ts_{P_{t,j},K}\leq Ct\).  Hence the boundary margin holds with exponent one and a universal coefficient.  The denominator does not deteriorate under the negative tilt.  Indeed, the pathwise derivative at zero is
\[
 \left.\partial_tW_{P_{t,j}}(1)\right|_{t=0}
 =-\frac{12}{180\sigma_{P_0,j}}
 \{j^{-4}-(j+1)^{-4}-g_j\}\geq c/j,
\]
because \(g_j>j^{-4}-(j+1)^{-4}\).  A second differentiation of the one-center first-order equation, using (1)--(2), is bounded uniformly in \(j\).  Since \(\delta_nK_n\to0\), the derivative remains nonnegative for \(0\leq t\leq\delta_n\), and hence \(W_{P_{t,j}}(1)\geq W_{P_0}(1)=1/12\).  Thus the denominator condition holds for every \(\underline w\leq1/12\).  The remaining nondegeneracy follows from the variance comparison below.  This proves class membership.

For completeness we record the stability calculation used for inference.  Along the path \(P_{t,j}\), differentiating the first-order center equations and using (9)--(11) bounds the first center derivative by \(CK^{3/2}\).  Differentiating the optimized risks by the envelope identity, and then differentiating once more, gives
\[
 \sup_{0\leq t\leq\delta_n}\max_{K<K_n}
 \frac{|\partial_t^2G_{P_{t,j}}(K)|}{\sigma_{P_0,K}}
 \leq CK_n^5. \tag{13}
\]
Here every density derivative is bounded by (1)--(2), every loss derivative is bounded by the cell radius times the center derivative, each inverse Hessian contributes at most \(CK^3\), and division by \(W_{P_{t,j}}(1)\) is valid by its \(1/24\) lower bound; collecting these displayed factors gives the conservative power \(K^5\).  The same differentiation of the optimized-loss influence function gives
\[
 \sup_{0\leq t\leq\delta_n}\max_{K<K_n}
 \frac{\|\partial_t\Delta\phi_{P_{t,j},K}\|_{L_2(P_0)}}{\sigma_{P_0,K}}
 \leq CK_n^5. \tag{14}
\]
Changing the integrating density from one to \(f_{t,j}\) adds at most \(Ct\) by (2).  The reverse triangle inequality for standard deviations and the covariance polarization identity applied to (14) therefore yield
\[
 \max_{K<K_n}\left|\frac{\sigma_{P_{t,j},K}}{\sigma_{P_0,K}}-1\right|
 +\sup_{K,L<K_n}|R_{P_{t,j}}(K,L)-R_{P_0}(K,L)|
 \leq CtK_n^5. \tag{15}
\]

The score of the path at zero is \(-s_{n,j}\).  The influence-function identity and the definition of \(s_{n,j}\) give
\[
 \left.\partial_tG_{P_{t,j}}(K)\right|_{t=0}
 =-E_{P_0}\{\Delta\phi_{P_0,K}s_{n,j}\}
 =-\sigma_{P_0,K}R_{P_0}(K,j). \tag{16}
\]
Taylor's theorem with (13) proves the asserted expansion and remainder.  At coordinate \(K=j\), subtracting the expansions for \(P_j\) and \(P_\ell\), and using \(R_{P_0}(j,j)=1\) and \(R_{P_0}(j,\ell)\leq0.28\), gives
\[
 \frac{|G_{P_j}(j)-G_{P_\ell}(j)|}{\sigma_{P_0,j}}
 \geq0.72\delta_n-2C\delta_n^2K_n^5.
\]
The last term is \(o(\delta_n)\), so one may take, for example, \(a_0=0.3\).

Finally, (1) and the elementary bound \(\log E e^{X}\leq E X+C\|X\|_\infty^2\) for centered bounded \(X\) give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j,P_0)
 =E_{P_j}\{-\delta_ns_{n,j}-\log Z_{\delta_n,j}\}
 \leq C\delta_n^2.
\]
Additivity of Kullback--Leibler divergence for independent products gives the claimed \(Cn\delta_n^2\) bound.

Set \(\nu_n=0\) in the local experiment \(\mathcal U_n\), and suppose the fixed class denominator satisfies \(\underline w\leq1/12\).  If \(\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\Xi_n(P^{(n)})\to0\), the band in \(\texttt{def:intrinsic-bootstrap-band}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n^{\#},\mathcal U_n)\).  On the event \(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\), whose probability tends to one uniformly over this experiment, its simultaneous standardized half-width obeys
\[
 \max_{1\leq K<K_n}\frac{q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}
 =q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\{1+o_{P^{(n)}}(1)\}
 \asymp_{P^{(n)}}w_n(P^{(n)}).
\]
Conversely, for every sequence of common \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable rectangular-band procedures in \(\texttt{def:rectangular-band-procedure}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\), there are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\), depending at most on \(\alpha\) and \(c_{\mathrm F}\) but independent of \(n\) and \(K_n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), some \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\left\{\max_{K\in J_n}\frac{\sqrt n\,h_{n,K}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}
 \geq c_0\sqrt{\log|J_n|}\right\}\geq c_1.
\]
Consequently the attainable and necessary radii over this noiseless causal experiment have the same intrinsic order
\[
 w_n(P^{(n)})/\sqrt n\asymp\sqrt{\log K_n/n}.
\]
statements.justification: The covariance-aware multiplier upper band and the multi-resolution information bound meet at the same intrinsic width on the explicit bounded-feature-safe causal experiment.
statements.gap: Existing fixed-target causal quantization, fixed-level quantizer geometry, and supplied-score bootstrap results do not jointly prove a matched covariance-aware upper and causal Fano lower radius for the adjacent-resolution process.
statements.consumer: A MineThatData report gains an honest rate-optimal rule for the entire resolution curve in the noiseless benchmark, while noisy matching is not claimed.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(P_0=P_{U,0}^{(n)}\), \(m=|J_n|\), and abbreviate row-law subscripts when no ambiguity can result.  We first verify that the assumed frontier condition supplies the growth hypotheses of the established membership and linearization theorems.  Direct integration over the \(K\) equal cells of the uniform quantizer gives
\[
 W_{P_0}(K)=\frac{1}{12K^2},\qquad s_{P_0,K}=\frac{1}{2K}.
 \tag{1}
\]
At the equal-cell codebook, differentiation of the distortion is legitimate because the two adjacent squared losses agree at every moving Voronoi boundary.  For \(K\geq2\), its Hessian is
\[
 H_K=\frac{1}{2K}
 \begin{pmatrix}
 3&-1&0&\cdots&0\\
 -1&2&-1&\ddots&\vdots\\
 0&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&0\\
 \vdots&\ddots&-1&2&-1\\
 0&\cdots&0&-1&3
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Indeed,
\[
 2Kx^{\mathsf T}H_Kx
 =\sum_{j=1}^{K-1}(x_{j+1}-x_j)^2+2x_1^2+2x_K^2.
 \tag{3}
\]
Since \(x_j=x_1+\sum_{a<j}(x_{a+1}-x_a)\), Cauchy--Schwarz implies
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^Kx_j^2
 \leq 2Kx_1^2+2K^2\sum_{a=1}^{K-1}(x_{a+1}-x_a)^2.
 \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4), together with Hessian continuity on a ball of radius proportional to the center spacing, permit the admissible choices
\[
 \lambda_{P_0,K}\asymp K^{-3},\qquad
 \kappa_{P_0,K}\asymp K^{-1},\qquad
 \alpha_{P_0,K}=1,qquad M_{P_0,K}=1.
 \tag{5}
\]
Here and below \(\lambda_{P_0,K}\) denotes this valid, possibly nonmaximal, quadratic-growth modulus; decreasing a valid modulus preserves the quadratic-growth inequality.  The margin assertion in (5) follows equation by equation from
\[
 P_0\!\left[\operatorname{dist}\{U,\mathcal B_{P_0,K}\}\leq t s_{P_0,K}\right]
 =(K-1)t/K\leq t,qquad 0<t\leq1.
 \tag{6}
\]
The exact covariance theorem gives
\[
 \sigma_{P_0,K}^2=V_K^{(0)}\asymp K^{-4},qquad
 w_n(P_0)\asymp\sqrt{\log K_n}.
 \tag{7}
\]
The first comparison in (7) follows directly by dividing the degree-eight numerator of \(V_K^{(0)}\) by its degree-twelve denominator; positivity is supplied by that theorem.

Because \(r_n=0\) in the stated experiment, (1), (5), and the definition of \(\delta^C\) yield
\[
 \delta^C_{P_0,K,n}\asymp K^2L_n.
 \tag{8}
\]
Take \(K^*=\lfloor K_n/2\rfloor\), which belongs to \(J_n\) eventually because \(K_n\to\infty\).  If the validity case in the definition of \(Q^C_{P_0,K^*,n}\) fails, then \(Q^C_{P_0,K^*,n}=1\).  The nonnegative \(Q^C\)-term in \(S^G\), (7), and the two Gaussian-width factors in \(\Xi_n\) then imply a lower bound of order \((K^*)^2\log K_n\), contradicting \(\Xi_n(P_0)\to0\).  In the validity case, (5), (6), and (8) give
\[
 \{Q^C_{P_0,K^*,n}\}^2
 \geq16M_{P_0,K^*}s_{P_0,K^*}^2
 \frac{\delta^C_{P_0,K^*,n}}{s_{P_0,K^*}}
 \geq cK^*L_n.
 \tag{9}
\]
All terms in \(S^G\) and \(\Xi_n\) are nonnegative.  Hence (7)--(9) imply
\[
 \Xi_n(P_0)
 \geq c(1+w_n(P_0))w_n(P_0)
 \frac{Q^C_{P_0,K^*,n}}{\sigma_{P_0,K^*}}
 \geq cK_n^{5/2}\log K_n\,L_n^{1/2}.
 \tag{10}
\]
Consequently the assumed convergence of \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_n}\Xi_n(P)\) implies
\[
 K_n^5\log^2K_n\,L_n\longrightarrow0,qquad
 K_n^5L_n\longrightarrow0,qquad
 \delta_nK_n^5\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{11}
\]
where the last implication uses
\[
 \delta_n=c_{\mathrm F}\sqrt{\frac{\log|J_n|}{n}}
 \leq c_{\mathrm F}L_n.
\]
Thus the hypotheses of \(\texttt{thm:fano-membership}\) and \(\texttt{thm:uniform-linearization}\) hold.  In particular, every law in \(\mathcal U_n\) is in \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), every coordinate variance is positive, and all divisions by \(W_P(1)\), \(\sigma_{P,K}\), and eventually \(\widehat\sigma_K\) below are valid.

For completeness, we also give a primitive sufficient regime for the abstract condition on \(\Xi_n\).  The density and covariance stability conclusions of \(\texttt{thm:fano-membership}\), the bound \(\|f_{n,j}-1\|_\infty=o(1)\), and comparison with the equal-cell codebook imply, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal U_n\) and \(K\leq K_n\),
\[
 W_P(K)\asymp K^{-2},\quad
 \lambda_{P,K}\asymp K^{-3},\quad
 s_{P,K}\asymp K^{-1},\quad
 \sigma_{P,K}\asymp K^{-2},\quad
 w_n(P)\asymp\sqrt{\log K_n}.
 \tag{12}
\]
The first comparison follows because \(1/2\leq f_{n,j}\leq3/2\) eventually: for every codebook its distortion under \(P_j\) lies between one half and three halves of its uniform-law distortion.  In the noiseless experiment \(\zeta_P=0\).  Since an optimized loss is bounded by \(s_{P,K}^2\), (12) and the definitions of \(\phi_W\), \(\phi_\rho\), and \(\Delta\phi\) give
\[
 \|\Delta\phi_{P,K}\|_\infty\leq CK^{-2},qquad
 \mathfrak E_n(P)\leq C.
 \tag{13}
\]
When the conditions displayed below hold, (11) follows, so the validity branch of \(Q^C\) applies uniformly.  Substitution into the definitions then gives
\[
 \delta^C_{P,K,n}\leq CK^2L_n,qquad
 Q^C_{P,K,n}\leq C(KL_n)^{1/2},
 \tag{14}
\]
because \((\delta^C)^2+s\delta^C\leq C(K^4L_n^2+KL_n)\leq CKL_n\).  Similarly, since \(r_n=0\),
\[
 R_{P,K,n}\leq CKL_n^2,quad
 E_{P,K,n}\leq C(L_n+KL_n^2),quad
 R^G_{P,K,n}\leq CKL_n^2,quad
 S^G_{P,K,n}\leq C(KL_n)^{1/2}.
 \tag{15}
\]
For example, the product term in \(R^G\) is bounded by
\[
 C(L_n+KL_n^2)L_n\leq C(L_n^2+KL_n^3)\leq CKL_n^2,
\]
and the remaining terms obey the same or a smaller bound by (12).  Equations (12)--(15) prove that the following three conditions are sufficient for \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal U_n}\Xi_n(P)\to0\):
\[
 \frac{\log^7(nK_n)}{n}\longrightarrow0,qquad
 \frac{K_n^3\sqrt{\log K_n}\log(nK_n)}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0,qquad
 K_n^{5/2}\log K_n
 \left\{\frac{\log(nK_n)}{n}\right\}^{1/4}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{16}
\]
This regime is nonvacuous.  If \(r_n=0\) and \(K_n=\lfloor n^\kappa\rfloor\) with \(0<\kappa<1/10\), the second and third expressions in (16) are respectively
\[
 O\!\left(n^{3\kappa-1/2}\log^{3/2}n\right)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 O\!\left(n^{5\kappa/2-1/4}\log^{5/4}n\right),
\]
and both converge to zero; the first expression also converges to zero.  Thus every such polynomial growth sequence satisfies the sufficient regime.

We next prove the upper conclusion.  Define the oracle maximum
\[
 T_n^0=
 \max_{1\leq K<K_n}\left|
 \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \frac{\Delta\phi_{P,K}(O_{n,i})}{\sigma_{P,K}}
 \right|.
 \tag{17}
\]
The summands in (17) are independent by the row sampling model, centered by the influence-function definitions, have unit coordinate variances by the definition of \(\sigma_{P,K}\) and score nondegeneracy, and have standardized sub-exponential envelope \(\mathfrak E_n(P)\).  The first term of \(\Xi_n(P)\) is exactly the sufficient scale in \(\texttt{lem:high-dimensional-gaussian-multiplier-approximation}\).  That lemma therefore approximates the law of \(T_n^0\) by the law of
\[
 M_P=\max_{1\leq K<K_n}|Z_{P,K}|
\]
and gives the corresponding conditional multiplier approximation for the oracle empirically centered scores, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal U_n\).

By \(\texttt{thm:uniform-linearization}\), relative variance consistency, and the remaining nonnegative terms in \(\Xi_n\),
\[
 \max_{K<K_n}\left|
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat G_K-G_P(K)\}}{\widehat\sigma_K}
 -\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \frac{\Delta\phi_{P,K}(O_{n,i})}{\sigma_{P,K}}
 \right|
 =o_P\!\left(\frac1{1+w_n(P)}\right).
 \tag{18}
\]
The same bound holds conditionally for replacing the oracle multiplier scores by \(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}/\widehat\sigma_K\).  The anti-concentration lemma, applied with \(p=K_n-1\), shows that a perturbation of the size in (18) changes the distribution function of the Gaussian maximum by \(o(1)\), because (12) gives \(w_n(P)\asymp\sqrt{\log K_n}\).  Combining the two oracle approximations with (18) yields
\[
 \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\left|
 P^n\!\left{
 \max_{K<K_n}\frac{\sqrt n|\widehat G_K-G_P(K)|}{\widehat\sigma_K}
 \leq t\right}
 -P\{T_n^{\#}\leq t\mid O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n}\}
 \right|=o_P(1)
 \tag{19}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal U_n\).  By the quantile-infimum definition of \(q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\), (19) gives simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\).  This is precisely \(\operatorname{Honest}_\alpha(B_n^{\#},\mathcal U_n)\).

We now locate the critical value.  A Gaussian union bound gives every fixed upper quantile of \(M_P\) the bound \(C_\alpha\sqrt{\log K_n}\).  For the reverse bound, the covariance stability in \(\texttt{thm:fano-membership}\) and the \(0.28\) separation in \(\texttt{thm:exact-covariance-packing}\) imply, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal U_n\),
\[
 R_P(K,L)\leq0.3,qquad K\ne L,quad K,L\in J_n,
 \tag{20}
\]
eventually.  We record the finite-dimensional comparison needed here.  Let \(X=(Z_{P,K}:K\in J_n)\), let \(\varepsilon_0,(\varepsilon_K:K\in J_n)\) be independent standard Gaussians, and put
\[
 Y_K=\sqrt{0.7}\,\varepsilon_K+\sqrt{0.3}\,\varepsilon_0.
\]
For a smooth nonincreasing approximation \(f\) to \(\mathbf1\{x\leq t\}\), set \(F(x)=\prod_{K\in J_n}f(x_K)\).  Along the centered Gaussian covariance interpolation from \(X\) to \(Y\), differentiating the finite-dimensional Gaussian density and integrating twice by parts gives
\[
 \frac{d}{du}\mathbb EF(X_u)
 =\frac12\sum_{K,L\in J_n}
 \{\operatorname{Cov}(Y_K,Y_L)-\operatorname{Cov}(X_K,X_L)\}
 \mathbb E\{\partial_{KL}F(X_u)\}.
 \tag{21}
\]
The diagonal summands vanish because both variances equal one.  For \(K\ne L\), the covariance difference is nonnegative by (20), while
\[
 \partial_{KL}F(x)=f'(x_K)f'(x_L)
 \prod_{a\ne K,L}f(x_a)\geq0.
\]
Integrating (21) and passing monotonically to the lower-orthant indicator proves
\[
 P\!\left(\max_{K\in J_n}X_K\leq t\right)
 \leq
 P\!\left(\max_{K\in J_n}Y_K\leq t\right).
 \tag{22}
\]
Fix \(c>0\) with \(c^2<1.4\) and take \(t=c\sqrt{\log m}\).  Conditional on \(|\varepsilon_0|\leq1\), independence and the elementary Gaussian tail bound obtained by one integration by parts give
\[
P\!\left(\max_KY_K\leq t\mid\varepsilon_0\right)
\leq
\Phi\!\left(\frac{t+\sqrt{0.3}}{\sqrt{0.7}}\right)^m
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{23}
\]
Indeed, writing \(\varphi\) for the standard Gaussian density, integration by parts yields
\[
 1-\Phi(x)\geq\frac{x}{1+x^2}\varphi(x),\qquad x>0.
\]
Consequently \(m\{1-\Phi((t+\sqrt{0.3})/\sqrt{0.7})\}\to\infty\) because \(c^2/1.4<1\), and \(\Phi(x)^m\leq\exp[-m\{1-\Phi(x)\}]\) proves (23).  Since \(P(|\varepsilon_0|>1)<1/2<1-\alpha\), and since \(\{M_P\leq t\}\subseteq\{\max_{K\in J_n}X_K\leq t\}\), (22)--(23) show that the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(M_P\) is at least \(c_\alpha\sqrt{\log m}\).  As \(m=K_n-8\) eventually, this lower bound and the union upper bound are both of order \(\sqrt{\log K_n}\).  They also show directly, together with the same upper bound on the expectation, that \(w_n(P)\asymp\sqrt{\log K_n}\).  The conditional approximation in (19) and Gaussian anti-concentration transfer these two quantile bounds to
\[
 q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\asymp_P w_n(P).
 \tag{24}
\]
Finally, \(\texttt{thm:uniform-linearization}\) gives
\[
 \max_{K<K_n}\left|\frac{\widehat\sigma_K}{\sigma_{P,K}}-1\right|=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 P\!\left(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\right)\longrightarrow1
 \tag{25}
\]
uniformly.  On the event in (25), (24) proves the asserted standardized half-width identity and order.

It remains to prove necessity.  For \(j\in J_n\), let
\[
 \theta_j=\{G_{P_j}(K):K\in J_n\},qquad
 d_\infty(\theta_j,\theta_\ell)
 =\max_{K\in J_n}
 \frac{|G_{P_j}(K)-G_{P_\ell}(K)|}{\sigma_{P_0,K}}.
\]
The separation and divergence conclusions of \(\texttt{thm:fano-membership}\) give
\[
 d_\infty(\theta_j,\theta_\ell)\geq a_0\delta_n
 \quad(j\ne\ell),qquad
 \frac1m\sum_{j\in J_n}
 \operatorname{KL}\{P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n}\}
 \leq Cc_{\mathrm F}^2\log m.
 \tag{26}
\]
Let the index \(J\) be uniform on \(J_n\), draw the sample from \(P_J^{\otimes n}\), and permit a decoder to use the declared \(V_n\).  Since \(V_n\) is independent of the index and sample under every law, adjoining it does not change any Kullback--Leibler divergence.  If \(Q_j\) is the joint sample-and-randomization law and \(\overline Q=m^{-1}\sum_jQ_j\), the log-sum inequality gives
\[
 I(J;O^n,V_n)
 =\frac1m\sum_j\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 \leq\frac1m\sum_j\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 \leq Cc_{\mathrm F}^2\log m.
 \tag{27}
\]
For every decoder \(\widehat J\), if \(p_e=P(\widehat J\ne J)\), the entropy chain rule and the fact that, conditional on an error, at most \(m-1\) indices remain possible imply
\[
 \log m=H(J)
 \leq I(J;O^n,V_n)+\log2+p_e\log m.
 \tag{28}
\]
Thus
\[
 \inf_{\widehat J}\frac1m\sum_{j\in J_n}Q_j(\widehat J\ne j)
 \geq1-Cc_{\mathrm F}^2-\frac{\log2}{\log m}.
 \tag{29}
\]
Choose the fixed \(c_{\mathrm F}\) sufficiently small that the right-hand side is eventually greater than \((1+\alpha)/2\), as permitted by its definition.

Now let \(B_n\) be any common measurable rectangular band satisfying the stated honesty condition.  Define \(\widehat J\) to be the smallest \(j\in J_n\) for which \(\theta_j\in B_n\), using a fixed default index when no such \(j\) exists.  If \(B_n\) covers \(\theta_j\) and
\[
 \max_{K\in J_n}\frac{h_{n,K}}{\sigma_{P_0,K}}
 <\frac{a_0\delta_n}{2},
 \tag{30}
\]
then the rectangle cannot contain any \(\theta_\ell\) with \(\ell\ne j\): otherwise every coordinate difference would be at most \(2h_{n,K}\), contradicting (26).  Therefore, under \(Q_j\), a decoding error is contained in the union of the noncoverage event and the complement of (30).  Uniform honesty and (29) yield
\[
 \frac1m\sum_{j\in J_n}
 P_j^{\otimes n}\!\left\{
 \max_{K\in J_n}\frac{h_{n,K}}{\sigma_{P_0,K}}
 \geq\frac{a_0\delta_n}{2}\right\}
 \geq \frac{1-\alpha}{2}-o(1).
 \tag{31}
\]
Hence some \(j\in J_n\) has the probability in (31) bounded below by a constant \(c_1>0\).  The uniform variance comparison in \(\texttt{thm:fano-membership}\) replaces \(\sigma_{P_0,K}\) by \(\sigma_{P_j,K}\) at a \(1+o(1)\) factor.  Since
\[
 \sqrt n\,\delta_n=c_{\mathrm F}\sqrt{\log m},
\]
this is exactly the claimed lower bound for suitable \(c_0,c_1>0\).  Combining it with (24)--(25) and \(m\asymp K_n\) proves that the attainable and necessary radii on the specified noiseless experiment are both of order
\[
 \frac{w_n(P)}{\sqrt n}\asymp\sqrt{\frac{\log K_n}{n}}.
\]

The witness proposition gives
\[
 G_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}}(K)
 =\frac{(12K^2)^{-1}-\{12(K+1)^2\}^{-1}}{1/12}
 =\frac{2K+1}{K^2(K+1)^2}=g_K.
\]
The exact diagonal formula has the uniform expansions
\[
 V_K^{(0)}=\frac8{5K^4}\{1+O(K^{-1})\},\qquad
 A_K=\frac{96}{K^2}\{1+O(K^{-1})\}.
\]
Both leading terms are nonnegative, so their sum retains relative error \(O(K^{-1})\) uniformly over \(\nu_n\in[0,1/4]\).  Therefore
\[
 \sigma_{P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)},K}^2
 =\left\{\frac8{5K^4}+\frac{96\nu_n^2}{K^2}\right\}\{1+o(1)\}.
\]
Since \(g_K=2K^{-3}\{1+O(K^{-1})\}\), if \(\nu_nK=O(1)\), then \(\sigma_K\asymp K^{-2}\) and \(g_K/\sigma_K\asymp K^{-1}\).  If \(\nu_nK\to\infty\), then \(\sigma_K\asymp\nu_n/K\) and \(g_K/\sigma_K\asymp(\nu_nK^2)^{-1}\).  Division is valid by witness score nondegeneracy.

If \(K_n=2\), the reported index set is the singleton \(\{1\}\).  The estimator and band definitions give
\[
 \widehat G_1=\widehat\rho(2)-\widehat\rho(1),\qquad
 I_{n,1}=[\widehat G_1\pm q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_1/\sqrt n]
\]
when \(\widehat\sigma_1>0\), with the declared conservative interval otherwise.  Since \(\widehat\rho(1)=1-\widehat W_1/\widehat W_1=0\), this is the one-coordinate ratio delta-method interval based on the fixed \(K=1,2\) corrected-risk influence-score difference.

statements.statement: Using def:heteroskedastic-extension-handle, characterize the weakest primitive conditions under which a nonuniform causal-feature law with heteroskedastic efficient residual admits an explicit cross-resolution semimetric, a diverging covariance-separated packing, and a corrected band whose upper radius and multi-resolution lower bound both equal its intrinsic Gaussian width. Determine when the width is \(\sqrt{\log K_n}\), \(\sqrt{\log\log K_n}\), or bounded.
statements.justification: The uniform arithmetic kernel is a sharp benchmark, but empirical causal-feature densities can induce qualitatively different dependence across resolutions.

\[

\]

statements.statement:
If \((Z_1,\ldots,Z_p)\) is a centered Gaussian vector with unit marginal variances and \(M=\max_{1\leq j\leq p}|Z_j|\), then, for every \(h>0\),
\[
 \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathbb P(|M-t|\leq h)
 \leq Ch\sqrt{\log(2p)},
\]
where \(C\) is numerical and does not depend on \(p\) or the covariance matrix.

sampling_model.design: Observational or randomized binary-treatment rows satisfying consistency, conditional exchangeability, and overlap; the exact lower-bound witness is a randomized trial.
sampling_model.units: For each row \(n\), \(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n}\) are independent draws from \(P^{(n)}\).

tldr: Adjacent causal-clustering resolutions share reoptimized codebooks and highly structured noise, so their joint inferential price is determined by the covariance geometry of their efficient scores rather than by the number of reported resolutions alone. The proposal computes the full uniform-law covariance through periodic Bernoulli polynomials and greatest-common-divisor identities, proves that the resulting process contains a linearly growing separated packing, derives a corrected cross-fitted band with intrinsic Gaussian-width radius, and matches it over the explicit local experiment \(\mathcal U_n\) with a genuine multi-resolution Fano lower bound whose tilted observed-data laws remain in one nondegenerate quantizer neighborhood.

project_justification.gap: Fixed-resolution causal \(k\)-means inference and quantizer geometry do not determine the covariance-aware minimax price of reporting an entire adjacent causal-distortion process. LiuPages2020 overlaps the optimizer- and distortion-performance-stability ingredient at fixed or level-by-level quantization, but its verified scope does not provide uniform \(K\le K_n\) control at shrinking adjacent-score scales, causal nuisance correction, joint adjacent efficient-score covariance, multiplier calibration, or a multi-resolution causal Fano lower bound. High-dimensional bootstrap theory treats supplied score arrays rather than this optimized causal process.
project_justification.niche: The exact cross-resolution kernel creates a theorem-level route to distinguish an intrinsic joint penalty from a crude coordinate-count penalty and to certify that penalty by a causal observed-data packing.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the arithmetic covariance and semimetric, controls optimized-risk and nuisance remainders at the associated Gaussian width, and proves matching upper and Fano lower bounds over the explicit local experiment \(\mathcal U_n\), while retaining only uniform linearization over the broader causal-quantizer class.
